record.paper_title: Using GANs for Sharing Networked Time Series Data: Challenges, Initial Promise, and Open Questions
record.original_question: How can synthetic-data generation methods such as DoppelGANger be extended to handle networking datasets whose behavior depends on causal interactions between stateful agents rather than only on isolated per-agent traces?

evidence.quote: Moreover, many networking datasets require significantly more complexity than DG is currently able to handle, such as causal interactions between stateful agents.

artifact.category_tag: Generative models for networked time series
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a system of $N$ stateful agents indexed by $i \in \{1,\dots,N\}$, each evolving in discrete time $t = 1,\dots,T$. Each agent $i$ has a hidden state $s^{(i)}_t \in \mathcal{S}$, an observable measurement $x^{(i)}_t \in \mathcal{X}$, and an associated time-invariant attribute $a^{(i)} \in \mathcal{A}$. The agents are coupled through a (possibly time-varying) interaction graph $G_t = (V, E_t)$ on $V = \{1,\dots,N\}$, and the joint dynamics satisfy a causal update rule of the form
$$ s^{(i)}_{t+1} = f\!\left(s^{(i)}_t,\; \{x^{(j)}_t : (j,i) \in E_t\},\; a^{(i)},\; \xi^{(i)}_t\right), \qquad x^{(i)}_t = g\!\left(s^{(i)}_t,\; \eta^{(i)}_t\right), $$
for some unknown stochastic functions $f, g$ and independent noise variables $\xi^{(i)}_t, \eta^{(i)}_t$. A dataset $\mathcal{D}$ consists of i.i.d. realizations of the full collection $\bigl(\{a^{(i)}\}_i, \{x^{(i)}_t\}_{i,t}\bigr)$.

Design a generative model — extending the architecture of generative adversarial networks for mixed attribute/time-series data (in which a generator first produces per-agent attributes from noise and then unrolls a per-agent recurrent network to emit a measurement sequence, trained against a pair of discriminators on attributes and on full trajectories) — that takes $\mathcal{D}$ as training data and produces synthetic samples whose joint distribution over $\bigl(\{a^{(i)}\}_i, \{x^{(i)}_t\}_{i,t}\bigr)$ faithfully reproduces:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the marginal per-agent attribute and trajectory distributions,
\item the cross-agent dependencies induced by the latent interaction graph $\{G_t\}$, and
\item the causal temporal dependencies in which agent $i$'s behavior at time $t+1$ depends on the behaviors of its neighbors at times $\leq t$.
\end{enumerate}
Provide an explicit architecture and training objective, together with theoretical guarantees (e.g., consistency, identifiability of the interaction structure, or fidelity bounds on multi-agent statistics) under stated assumptions on $f, g$ and the graph process. In particular, determine whether such guarantees are achievable when the graph $\{G_t\}$ is unobserved and must be inferred from the data alone.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of extending DoppelGANger-style synthetic data generation to multi-agent networking datasets with causal inter-agent dependencies is described as an open challenge. Subsequent work has explored related directions (e.g., graph-based or multi-agent time-series GANs), but no published method to date provides a comprehensive, theoretically-grounded extension that handles causal interactions among stateful agents in networking traces. The problem appears to remain open.
